profile.summary: RNAGenesis is an RNA foundation model that handles sequence representation, structure prediction and sequence design in one framework. A BERT-style encoder, pretrained with masked RNA modelling on non-coding RNAs, turns an RNA sequence into embeddings; a query-based compression step maps those into a short latent code, and a diffusion model generates new latent codes that a decoder turns back into sequences. It is used both to score or classify RNAs after fine-tuning and to design new ones, such as aptamers and CRISPR sgRNA scaffolds.

summary_quotes.text: a Generalist RNA foundation model that integrates sequence representation, structural prediction, and de novo functional design within a single generative framework
Trained on diverse clustered non-coding RNAs, RNAGenesis leverages a BERT-style encoder, query-based latent compression, and a diffusion-guided decoder
unifies sequence understanding, *de novo* RNA design, and 3D structure prediction through a latent diffusion framework
RNAGenesis enables functional RNA design, including aptamers targeting IGFBP3 and structurally constrained sgRNA scaffolds

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The repository's pretraining configuration for the stage-one encoder uses single-nucleotide embeddings of width 1,280, six parallel convolutional layers with kernels 3 to 13 whose outputs are summed with those embeddings, and 32 bidirectional Transformer blocks with 20 attention heads, RoPE and SwiGLU feed-forward layers. Training is masked RNA modelling: 30% of positions are selected and the loss is cross-entropy on those positions only. The repository notes that masking happens before the convolutional embeddings, so the masked bases cannot leak through the convolutions. No source read says which configuration the released Zenodo and Hugging Face weights use. The repository tree also holds two files whose names contain 6layers_16heads_128embedsize. For generation, the encoder output is compressed into a latent code, a diffusion model samples new latent codes, and a decoder produces sequences. Sampling can be steered at inference time by a classifier gradient or by beam search.

quotes.text: Single-nucleotide embeddings of width 1,280, including IUPAC and special tokens.
Six parallel stride-one, same-padded Conv1D layers with kernels `3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13`; their outputs are summed with the nucleotide embeddings.
32 bidirectional Transformer blocks, 20 attention heads, RoPE, pre-LayerNorm, SwiGLU FFNs of intermediate width 3,413, and residual connections.
Each nucleotide is independently selected with probability `0.30`.
**Masking happens before both the convolutional embeddings and the Transformer**, so the original selected bases cannot leak through the CNN.
a diffusion-guided decoder enhanced by inference-time alignment with gradient guidance and beam search strategies

sections.title: What it is used for
sections.body: Two routes are documented. For understanding tasks, the pretrained encoder is fine-tuned: the repository's example adds LoRA adapters, averages the valid nucleotide embeddings and trains an MLP head for 13 ncRNA classes. For design, generation.py samples sequences from a diffusion checkpoint, with aptamer and sgRNA checkpoints given as examples, optionally with classifier guidance or beam search. A separate module fine-tunes the encoder for 3D structure prediction.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Weights are distributed in two places. Zenodo record 15203813 holds checkpoints.zip and configs.zip, plus the ProGen2 base and small decoders, published on 2025-04-12 under CC BY 4.0. The encoder alone is on Hugging Face as Zaixi/RNAGenesis (revision d8a42130 when read), where the card declares cc-by-nc-4.0 and access is gated. A result should name which route and which diffusion checkpoint directory was used, since the generation commands differ by task.

run_guide.summary: Install the repository environment, download the released checkpoints from Zenodo and sample sgRNA scaffold sequences with the diffusion model.
prerequisites: conda, for the environment; the alternative route pins python=3.8.13 and torch==2.1.2.
A GPU. The README states one generation run takes about 5 hours on one A100; no GPU memory figure is given.
About 31.7 GB of download for the four Zenodo archives (checkpoints.zip 14.5 GB, configs.zip 15.3 GB, progen2-base.zip 1.4 GB, progen2-small.zip 0.56 GB), plus disk space to unzip them.
Code is MIT licensed; the Zenodo archives are CC BY 4.0.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/zaixizhang/RNAGenesis.git
cd RNAGenesis
git checkout --detach 393dbc15d2146bd9475240756b83e767b8b1d45b
steps.explanation: The README gives no clone command; the clone, cd and checkout lines are added to get the repository at the commit this page was written from.

quotes.text: **RNAGenesis** is a compact yet powerful RNA foundation model

steps.title: Create the environment
steps.shell:
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate rnagenesis
steps.explanation: Option 1 in the README builds the environment from the bundled YAML file.

steps.title: Download and extract the weights
steps.shell:
mkdir -p checkpoints
mkdir -p configs

wget -O checkpoints.zip "https://zenodo.org/records/15203813/files/checkpoints.zip?download=1"
wget -O configs.zip "https://zenodo.org/records/15203813/files/configs.zip?download=1"
wget -O progen2-base.zip "https://zenodo.org/records/15203813/files/progen2-base.zip?download=1"
wget -O progen2-small.zip "https://zenodo.org/records/15203813/files/progen2-small.zip?download=1"

unzip checkpoints.zip -d checkpoints/
unzip configs.zip -d configs/
unzip progen2-base.zip -d models/autoencoder/decoder/checkpoints/progen2-base/
unzip progen2-small.zip -d models/autoencoder/decoder/checkpoints/progen2-small/
steps.explanation: The README's download block, with its clean-up lines left out so the archives are kept.

steps.explanation: The README's sgRNA generation command, unchanged. For aptamers the README uses --max_seq_len 37 with checkpoints/Aptamer/diffusion.

outputs: Generated sequence files under the folder named by --superfolder and --mid_folder, which the README sets to generation_sequences and RNAGenesis_sgRNA. The README does not describe the file format.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The generation command depends on the paths inside the Zenodo archives (configs/rnagenesis/autoencoder, checkpoints/sgRNA/diffusion), which were not inspected.
The README's guidance example points at configs/rangenesis/classifier/..., which looks like a typo in the repository; it is not reproduced here.
The README states one full generation run takes about 5 hours on one A100 GPU.

notes: Two repositories carry this model: zaixizhang/RNAGenesis (used here, the newer one, MIT, last pushed 2026-10-01) and myuxu/RNAGenesis (an earlier copy of the same README). The Zenodo record is titled 'RNAGeneiss', a misspelling in the record metadata. The Hugging Face card could not be read because the repository is gated, so the weights licence there comes from the API cardData field only. The RNAGym fitness leaderboard row names only 'RNAGenesis', with no checkpoint or revision. The Hugging Face files are named for xTrimoPGLM modelling code, which the repository does not explain; this was not pursued. The Hugging Face row's 'released' is the repository creation date, not a stated release date.
